title: Ephemeral priority bands and graceful fallback modes for overload control
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Proposal and implementation ticket for a complementary load-shedding mechanism that uses short-lived (ephemeral) priority bands, soft admission control, and graceful degradation modes. The goal is to reduce tail latency and keep SLOs during sudden capacity pressure or partial-region outages by: 1) assigning ephemeral priority bands per request at the edge (high/normal/low/bench), 2) implementing soft admission (best-effort admission path that can return cached stubs, partial completions, or condensed responses), 3) per-tenant circuit breakers that open on SLO breach signals, and 4) automated multi-region reroute when regional latency or error SLOs are violated. This ticket covers design, implementation plan, telemetry, runbook, and canary rollout for the dispatcher and admission controller changes.
design_decisions: Use ephemeral bands scored by tokenized cost + SLA tier rather than static priority queues to avoid long-lived starvation
Soft admission path returns one of: cached completion, condensed summary (length-limited), or a structured error with suggested retry-after — prefer partial outputs over hard failures
Circuit breakers are tenant-scoped and evaluated on a moving-window of p95 latency and error rate; breaker has two thresholds (soft, hard) to trigger degradation vs full reject

Multi-region failover uses SLO-driven routing: if region p95 > SLO for 3 consecutive minutes AND error-rate spike > 2x baseline, shift 30-70% traffic to healthy region with gradual ramp and canary checks
Admission control will expose a hint header X-RI-Shed-Mode for downstream services and SDKs to enable client-side fallback UX
implementation_notes: Edge: add ephemeral band assignment module in edge-proxy (rust) — score uses tenant tier, request weight, model seq-length estimate
Dispatcher: implement dual-path admission: guaranteed lane (for reserved capacity), best-effort lane (can be post-processed), and bench lane (low-priority background execution)
Runtime: soft-timeout handler that cancels long-running generation but returns best-effort prefix from KV cache or partial decode
Circuit breaker: use existing circuit framework but introduce a two-state breaker (degrade, open) with translational mapping to admission policies
Metrics: emit shed_decisions{band,reason,tenant} and shed_outcome{served_degraded,served_full,rejected} for SRE dashboards
progress_updates: 2026-02-18 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial proposal captured and reviewed with SRE and Runtime teams. Identified primary KPIs: p95 latency, tail token latency, shed_rate, and regression in output quality for degraded responses. Linked design doc.

2026-02-24 - Marcus Lee: Prototype ephemeral band assignment implemented in edge-proxy branch feat/ephemeral-bands. Basic scoring function: 40% token_estimate + 40% tenant_tier + 20% model_cost. Unit tests added.

2026-02-28 - SRE review (Evan Morales): Raised concern about metric cardinality for per-tenant shed events; agreed to roll metrics up to tenant_tier in initial rollout. Action: reduce high-cardinality tags.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Lee: Dispatcher admission paths merged to feature flag behind runtime-1.22.canary. Added soft-timeout plumbing in runtime worker; returns cached prefix when available. Integration tests passing in staging.

2026-03-05 - Product (Lina Torres): Reviewed UX for SDK: will surface X-RI-Shed-Mode and suggest client fallback to local summarizer when mode=degraded. Requesting copy for docs and deprecation policy for older SDKs
risks_and_mitigations: Output quality regressions when returning condensed summaries: mitigation = sample-based eval comparing degraded vs full outputs and blocking on >3% regression for critical prompt sets
Incorrect band assignment causing unfair rejection: mitigation = shadow mode for 48h with traffic replay and per-tenant fairness metrics before full enable
Metric explosion from per-request tags: mitigation = aggregate to tier-level and implement sampling for high-cardinality tenants
Cascading failover causing overload in secondary region: mitigation = conservative ramp (30% immediate, then 15% per min), circuit-breaker backpressure across regions
testing_plan: Shadow rollout in us-west-2 for 72 hours with full telemetry; compare shed_outcome rates and quality evals against control cohort
Canary enable on 5% of production traffic with kill-switch per-tenant and global override
Inject synthetic overload in staging (SLO breach for 5 minutes) to validate multi-region reroute and ramp behavior
Automated e2e tests to assert X-RI-Shed-Mode header semantics and SDK fallbacks
